_note: The third heart events (data/events/heart_<villager>_6.json): one scene per villager when their heart band first reaches 6 and the farmer talks to them, after the band 5 one. One part per villager, started at its id (Hachiro's has a second part, hachiro_strike, after the farmer's hammer blow; Fumi's looks back on fumi_honest from her band 3 scene, Ichiro's on ichiro_kiln from his band 5 one, Genzo's on genzo_jizo from his, Haru's on haru_go from her band 5 answer, Shige's on shige_share from his, Nana's on nana_beside from her band 5 answer). Our own scenes.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: My son wrote back. He wants me to come and live in the city with him. An apartment with an elevator, he says.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: He means well. He frets about the shrine stairs, and the winters, and me alone in that house.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: But I wrote that the village needs its old woman. And the farm on the hill needs somebody to nag it.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: But I wrote that I have a grandchild on the hill now. Somebody has to see they eat properly.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: My husband planted the persimmon by the shrine the year we married. I mean to see it fruit a few more times.

choices.text: I'll help you up the stairs.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: So am I, child. So am I. Now, I told him you'd add a line to my next letter. In your best hand.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Ha! I'll hold you to that, every step. ...Thank you. That's what I'll tell him.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: Close your eyes! ...Okay, open. It's a carp streamer! I made it. Mostly. Mom did the sewing bit.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: See? It's black, with one white spot. You know who that is.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: Nobody else would get it. Only you and me have seen him up close.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: It's for the promise. We both kept it, so now he can fly instead of getting caught.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: Our house hasn't got a pole. But your farm has the whole hill's wind. So... it's yours. If you want it.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: I'll put it up by the house, on the tallest pole I can find.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: Tall enough the real one can see it from the pond! I'll check it every time I come to help.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: I was tidying Father's last ledger. On the final page, under the sums, he'd written something.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: 'Sayo will do it her own way. Let her.' That's all. He never once said it to my face.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: All those years of thinking I was only minding his store. He'd already handed it over.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Every morning I look up at the new sign and think: he already knew. He just let me find out.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: So I've started a new ledger. My own. Page one, line one.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: ...I wrote your name first. Not for anything you owe. Just so the book starts with a friend.

choices.text: Better keep my tab small, then.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Don't look at me like that. I'll go red, and red is for the sign.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Ha! Too late, I've already charged you for the ink. ...I'm joking. Mostly.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: You. Pick up that hammer. The small one.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: Every year I forge one sickle and leave it at my teacher's grave. It's the only gift he ever liked.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: My arm shakes a little now, on the last blows. Nobody notices but me. And now you.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: Strike where I point. Once. Not hard. Straight.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: ...Hm. Straight. Teacher would have grumbled, and kept it.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: A blade remembers every hand on it. This one will remember yours.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: That bell by your door still rings low in the mornings? Good. Your house is learning your hours.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: Next year you strike twice. Don't make a fuss. Go on, the field won't hoe itself.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Pull the shutter behind you? I want to show you something before anyone else comes in.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: My mother's kettle. It cracked the winter she died, and it has sat in a box ever since.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Hachiro mended it last week. He wouldn't take a coin for it. He said it was owed to her.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: You told me true about the bean paste, so here's mine: I had Hachiro mend it because of you.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: The first cup from it should go to someone who matters. I've thought about it a long while.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Then hold the cup with both hands. ...There. Now it's a kettle again, not a keepsake.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Tome gets the second. She'll grumble, but she'd agree with me. Now drink, before I go red.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: ...Hold out your hand. Palm up.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: The first piece from the new kiln. The very first. It rang before it had cooled.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: I never said thanks for coming to see the smoke. So. First piece. That's thanks.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: You dug the clay with me. My father's rule: whoever digs gets the first piece.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: There's a mark in the clay by the kiln door. My father's. Mine. I left room for one more, and I never knew for whom.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: ...Now I do. Press your thumb in, if you want. It's your kiln as much as mine.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Press hard, so it holds. ...It'll outlast the both of us.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Ha. A small one, then. Clay doesn't care. It keeps whatever you give it.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Three marks on one kiln. Hm. ...That's a family. Don't tell Fumi I used the word.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Stay a moment. The harvest is in, and I have something to finish.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: The straw from your seed rice came out clean and long. Better than my own, and I'll deny I said so.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: My wife always braided the first straw into a rope for the jizo. I never learned how. I let the jizo go without.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Every autumn I stood and held the cloth while my wife tied the bibs. This year I stood and watched you tie them. It felt the same. Almost the same.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: So I braided one, badly, with these old fingers. It took me all week. It's a straw rope for the jizo, the way she made it.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: I'd like it tied on by two pairs of hands. Mine, and the ones I trust to keep the lane when I can't climb it anymore.

choices.text: It's yours to tie. I'll hold it.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Over, under, pull. ...There. Your end is the straighter one. Don't tell the jizo.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Hm. Hold it steady, then. ...Done. Not one bad knot. She would have called that a miracle.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: The rice grows well for you. And the lane is red and tied again. ...I think I can stop counting the years now.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Wait, don't go yet. I want to see your face when you hear this.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: The city shop wrote again. Not to fetch me this time. They want my sandals on their shelf, with a tag, and I would post them from Sayo's store.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: You said Kaminoda would miss me. It does. Genzo has said 'Haru, the rack' eleven times this week, just to hear himself say it.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: You said to go if it called me. It called. Then I read this letter and found I could answer it from here. Funny. Nobody holding the door is what let me stay.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: They asked what the tag should say. The place, or my name? I have written both on scraps and thrown both away.

choices.text: Kaminoda. Let them find the hamlet.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Kaminoda, in small black ink, with the bamboo hill under it. Then they'll have to come up the lane to see where the straw grew.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: My name, on a tag, in a city shop... I'll have to braid very straight, then. Everybody will check.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: One more thing. I wave from the lookout every afternoon, and you never wave back. Tomorrow, wave. Then I'll know it isn't only the wind.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Come and look before the light goes. It came up. All of it.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: The vine by the fence ran the whole length of the rail this summer. Four pumpkins. Nana cried over the first one, and I studied the sky very hard.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: She would have looked for them at the fence, and there they were. Eight years in a tin, and the soil still remembered the seed.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Yours came up too, didn't it? Half and half, and both patches took. I told Nana that is how a grower sleeps at night.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Even the crows keep off. Nana swears it's her scarecrow. I let her swear. Now, a grower's question. The first pumpkin: the pot, or the tin?

choices.text: The pot. Eat it her way.
The tin. Save the seed first.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: The pot. Sweet, far too sweet, three bowls each. She would have laughed to see me go back for a fourth.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: The tin first... Yes. Seed first, supper after. That is how she did it, and that tin should never sit empty again.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Supper is at six. Nana will make the pot either way. Come hungry, and don't tell her I asked.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Captain's a frog now! He sang all night in the ditch. Dad says it's the loudest thing he ever heard, and he has heard Kota.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: I drew my sky map again, bigger, on an old bedsheet. Dad held the corner while I pinned it to the barn wall. Then he looked at it for ages and didn't say anything.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: He found the big steady star and said, 'Too bright.' Then he stood there till the hens complained. That's how I know he likes it.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: He found the two stars blinking beside each other and said, 'Well. They blink at each other.' Then he went to feed the hens. Nobody feeds hens that slowly unless they're thinking.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: There's one space left on the map. A star for you! But I can't decide where it goes. Close to Dad's, or far out by itself over your field?

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Next to Dad's. Then he'll have somebody to say 'too bright' to. Yes. I'm drawing it with my best pencil.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Over your field, so you can look up from your rows and find it. ...That's a good one. I'll make it a little bit twinkly.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Dad says I can stay up till all the stars are out, if I wear my scarf. Wave at the sky tonight when you're out in your field? I'll know which wave is yours.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: There you are. I've been waiting on the shore since the mist came up.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: I wanted to tell you before anyone else hears it from Kota.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: You told me I'd still be me without the ferry. So I let the landing go. Then I found I wanted to pole across once more anyway, just for myself.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: You said someone would need the slow way. Last night the bell rang. An old peddler, soaked to the knees. I took him across by lantern light.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: The boat's never had a name. Father said a boat with a name gets proud and tips over. I think it's time anyway.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: ...Then it's Tatsu's boat again. He'd grumble. He'd be pleased.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: A new name, then. I'll paint it on tonight and tell you when it's dry. No peeking.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: One more thing. The first crossing of the morning is mine to give. From now on it's yours, whenever you want it.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: You're here! I've been waiting by the new fortune box since the gravel was raked.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: I led the New Year rite. Alone. The whole village heard every word.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: And I never once looked at my sleeve. Tome says the words were mine all along. The ink is still there, though. I'm keeping it.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: You made me say them to you on this step. So at midnight, I just... said them to you again, in my head. It worked.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Grandfather's last box of fortunes is new paper now. Somebody has to draw the very first one.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Great blessing! ...For you, of course. I definitely didn't put three in the front.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Both hands on the box, then. ...Great blessing. One slip, two people. Tome would say that means something.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: From now on, the first fortune every New Year is yours. That's a shrine keeper's promise.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: There you are. Come and look. The first bolt of the year is dry.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Sayo sold the whole first batch in two days. Two days. The city shop took a month.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Mother's cranes, every one. Kiku cried when she saw them. Then she bought three.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: My wildflower stencil. People keep asking what the flowers are. I tell them: the ones by the lane.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: I kept one length back for you. For a noren on your door. Which pattern?

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: The rows of your field. Straight lines are the hardest to dye true. ...Fine. For you, they'll be true.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Then every morning you'll walk out under the flowers from the lane. I like thinking of that.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: One more thing. From now on the first cloth out of every new vat is yours. That's how a dyer says it.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: You'll never guess what was in the morning bag. A reply from head office. About me.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: I read it twice on the step of the post office. Then once more to the hens. They had no opinion.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: They're keeping the rounds on foot. Someone sent them a letter signed by every house in the valley. I carried it myself. I didn't peek. Much.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: The van's mine, on one rule I set: I park at the bridge and walk the last stretch to every door. They said yes.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: I've carried ten thousand letters and never written one. So I wrote one. To you.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Now? In front of me? ...I'll look at the pond. Tell me when you've finished. Don't read it out loud.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Sealed! Someone after my own heart. Some letters are better as letters.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: From tomorrow your farm is the first stop on my round. Whatever comes for you, you'll have it before the dew's dry.
